metadata.title: Order of Operations and BODMAS
metadata.description: Follow BODMAS correctly, including left-to-right precedence for division/multiplication and addition/subtraction.
metadata.teachingApproach: Read the structure; respect precedence; work left to right at equal levels; check the magnitude.
metadata.sourceScope: R.S. Aggarwal, Quantitative Aptitude for Competitive Examinations, Chapter 4 “Simplification,” printed pages 95–179. Approved scope: Teach the chapter’s BODMAS sequence: evaluate brackets first, then “of” where it means multiplication, then division and multiplication from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right. Explain that multiplication and division share precedence, as do addition and subtraction; do not incorrectly process every division before every multiplication. Cover integers, decimals, powers, and mixed operation chains at the level used in the chapter. Show a written line-by-line method, where a common tempting left-to-right shortcut fails, and how to estimate or substitute back to check. A learner should be able to identify the next legal operation, preserve the original grouping, and calculate without changing order.

content.text:
A long arithmetic expression is a set of instructions, not a list of operations that can be done in any order. The same numbers can produce different answers when the order changes, so first identify the structure and only then calculate.

Use BODMAS as a guide: brackets first; “of” when it means multiplication by a quantity; powers; division and multiplication from left to right; then addition and subtraction from left to right. The key detail is that D and M share a level, as do A and S. BODMAS does not mean “do every division before every multiplication.”

Before writing a line of working, circle the brackets, underline powers, and mark the first operation at each precedence level. This visual scan takes a few seconds and prevents most order-of-operations errors.

First resolve any grouping symbols, starting with the innermost bracket. Evaluate powers before the ordinary multiplication/division and addition/subtraction steps. Where the chapter writes “of,” treat it as multiplication by the stated quantity before proceeding to division in that expression.

For 18 + 24 ÷ 6 × 3 − 2², calculate 2²=4 first. Then work left to right through division and multiplication: 24÷6=4, then 4×3=12. Finally handle addition and subtraction from the left: 18+12−4=26. Do not subtract 4 from 18 first just because it appears nearby; addition and subtraction come after the product/quotient chain.

A useful check is to rewrite one legal operation at a time on a new line. If an intermediate line changes grouping or skips an operation that has higher precedence, stop and correct it before continuing.

A reliable sequence is to simplify one small part, rewrite the remaining expression, and repeat. Avoid doing several mental changes at once: each new line should be equivalent to the line above it, so the process can be checked locally.

hints: Division and multiplication have equal precedence; start with the one farther left.
Calculate 12÷3, then multiply by 2 before subtracting.
inlineData.explanation: 12÷3=4, then 4×2=8. Finally 20−8=12. Division and multiplication have equal precedence, so the leftmost one is performed first. Check that the expression inside the subtraction evaluates to 8. Correct option: B.

content.text:
Division and multiplication have equal precedence, so read them from left to right. In 20−12÷3×2, calculate 12÷3=4, then 4×2=8, and only then subtract: 20−8=12. Doing 3×2 first would change the expression and is not allowed without brackets.

On the retry, point to the leftmost operation among division and multiplication before you calculate.

A common wrong route is to combine 3×2 before dividing. That is only allowed if the original expression has a bracket around 3×2. Without such grouping, the left-to-right rule decides the order.

hints: Do the leftmost of division and multiplication first.
18÷3=6, then multiply by 2 and subtract from 30.
inlineData.explanation: 18÷3=6; 6×2=12; 30−12=18. This follows the same precedence rule: complete powers/grouping, do division and multiplication left-to-right, and leave subtraction until the end. Correct option: D. Correct option: A.

content.text:
Brackets change which quantity is used in the next operation. In 48÷6×(3+1)−5, the bracket is 4, so the expression becomes 48÷6×4−5. Continue left to right: 48÷6=8, then 8×4=32, then 32−5=27.

Compare that with 48÷(6×4)−5. Here the whole product 6×4=24 is the divisor, so 48÷24−5=−3. The numbers are similar, but the grouping is different. Never remove brackets until you know that doing so preserves the expression.

When uncertain, write the value of a bracket explicitly and substitute that value into the original expression. This prevents a correct inner calculation from being placed in the wrong part of the expression.

Brackets are not decoration; they define the input to the next operation. The safest habit is to replace a completed bracket with parentheses around its answer first, then continue with the surrounding expression.

hints: Treat “of” as multiplication and do that part before the division here.
Find 2×12, divide the result by 6, then add 5.
inlineData.explanation: “Of” is treated as multiplication here: 2×12=24, then 24÷6=4, and 5+4=9. Do not add 5 before evaluating the product and quotient. Correct option: C.

content.text:
When “of” appears, identify the number and the quantity it applies to. Evaluate that multiplication first in the convention used by this chapter, then continue through division and addition/subtraction. For 7+3 of 8÷4, calculate 3×8=24, 24÷4=6, and 7+6=13.

The retry uses new values to check whether you can apply the same sequence without copying the previous result.

Do not treat “of” as a vague word; identify exactly what quantity is being multiplied. Once that product is found, resume the stated order for the remaining operations.

inlineData.explanation: 3×8=24, 24÷4=6, and 7+6=13. This follows the same precedence rule: complete powers/grouping, do division and multiplication left-to-right, and leave subtraction until the end. Correct option: C. Correct option: D.

content.text:
The word “of” is treated as multiplication in these aptitude expressions. For 5 + 2 of 12 ÷ 6, evaluate 2×12=24, then divide 24÷6=4, then add 5 to get 9. Keep the “of” quantity together long enough to evaluate it properly.

Fraction bars also act as grouping symbols. In (a+b)/c, the entire numerator a+b is divided by c. Likewise, a/(b+c) has the entire b+c as its denominator. Those forms are not interchangeable with a+b/c or a/b+c.

Estimate the size before accepting a result. For example, 48÷6×4 is 8×4=32, which is larger than 48÷6=8. If your result became much smaller, you may have grouped the expression differently or performed addition/subtraction too early.

For long chains, put multiplication/division on one line and addition/subtraction on the next. This separates the precedence levels and makes it easier to see whether an operation was performed too early.

hints: Then divide 72 by 8, multiply by 5, and subtract 6.
inlineData.explanation: First (2+3)=5. Then 72÷8=9 and 9×5=45; finally 45−6=39. The bracket is evaluated before the division/multiplication chain. Correct option: A.

content.text:
Keep any bracket intact until its value is known. For 72÷8×(2+3)−6, first find 2+3=5, then divide 72 by 8, multiply by 5, and subtract 6. Do not multiply 8 by 5; the original expression has no bracket around 8×(2+3).

Use this same “resolve grouping, then left-to-right at equal levels” routine on the retry.

Check the divisor carefully: in 72÷8×5 the divisor is 8, not 8×5. A divisor is grouped with the following factor only when the expression explicitly places them together.

hints: Evaluate the bracket, then continue left to right through division and multiplication.
inlineData.explanation: (4+2)=6; 63÷7=9; 9×6−8=46. This follows the same precedence rule: complete powers/grouping, do division and multiplication left-to-right, and leave subtraction until the end. Correct option: A. Correct option: C.

content.text:
You have completed Order of Operations and BODMAS.

Remember three checks: resolve grouping first; treat division/multiplication as equal and work left to right; treat addition/subtraction as equal and work left to right. Powers and the chapter’s “of” convention must be handled before the remaining lower-precedence operations.

If a result seems implausible, revisit the last operation you performed and compare it with the original expression. A correct calculation must preserve the original grouping at every line.

Powers apply to the expression directly attached to them. Thus −3² means −(3²)=−9, while (−3)²=(−3)×(−3)=9 because the negative sign is inside the brackets and is squared too.

Now combine this with precedence in 72÷8×3−4². First, 4²=16. Next, 72÷8=9, then 9×3=27. Finally, 27−16=11. Do not read the whole expression strictly left to right from its first symbol; resolve the power first, then follow the remaining precedence levels.

For a final reasonableness check, compare the result with the sizes of the pieces. Here the product is 27 and the square is 16, so a positive result of 11 is plausible.

This sign rule also matters with variables: −a² means −(a²), while (−a)² is a². When in doubt, rewrite the expression with explicit parentheses before calculating.

hints: Evaluate the power first, then division and multiplication left to right.
inlineData.explanation: 4²=16 first. Next 72÷8=9, and 9×3=27. Finish with 27−16=11. The square must be evaluated before the final subtraction. Correct option: B.

content.text:
A power is evaluated before an outside multiplication, division, addition or subtraction. Keep the sign distinction visible: −5²=−25, but (−5)²=25. After the power is settled, work left to right through division/multiplication and finish with addition/subtraction.

Before submitting, ask yourself what is squared: only the number, or the number together with its sign inside brackets?

If a power is attached only to a positive numeral, an outside minus remains outside the power. This is why the two expressions −5² and (−5)² have opposite signs.

hints: Evaluate the square first, then divide and multiply from the left.
inlineData.explanation: 5²=25; 90÷10=9; 9×4=36; 36−25=11. This follows the same precedence rule: complete powers/grouping, do division and multiplication left-to-right, and leave subtraction until the end. Correct option: B. Correct option: D.
